subject: Streaming feature enablement — schema gate & implementation play
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@pulsehealth.io>, PulseHealth Integrations <integrations@pulsehealth.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming feature enablement — schema gate & implementation play

Hi Elena / integration team,

Great to meet virtually this morning — thanks for the time. Per our handoff call with PulseHealth CSMs and engineering, this thread will be our primary implementation lane for streaming + function/tool calling + structured JSON output (the "schema gate") so nothing falls through the cracks.

High-level goals:
- Deliver a production-grade streaming integration for real-time assistance within PulseHealth (max latency target: 250ms median for 512-token windows).
- Enable function/tool calling for appointment lookups and EHR queries.
- Enforce structured outputs via a JSON schema validation step so downstream services can safely parse responses.

Proposed 4-week play (quick):
1) Week 0 (this week): confirm stakeholders, firewall/IP allowlist, sample payloads, and access (API key + staging model endpoint).
2) Week 1: schema finalization + small tech readout; run a smoke streaming session.
3) Week 2: function/tool calling tests (sandbox) and auth validation.
4) Week 3: performance run and rollout checklist; production cutover plan.

Immediate asks from PulseHealth: please reply with
- primary platform engineer and best contact for VPN/firewall rules
- sample request/response payloads (if you have any existing JSON contracts)
- whether you require on-prem agent deployment or if public-hosted endpoints are acceptable for staging

Attachments: pulse_schema_v1.json (draft JSON schema), integration_matrix.xlsx (integration matrix and checklist)

I'll set a 60-minute technical session for early next week; Rishi will lead the kernel/latency conversation and Priyom will own schema alignment.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Elena Park <elena.park@pulsehealth.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, PulseHealth Integrations <integrations@pulsehealth.io>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@pulsehealth.io>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming feature enablement — schema gate & implementation play

Thanks Mina — this looks good.

Quick answers: Samir Rao (cc'd) will be our primary platform engineer; he's joining the thread. We can provide a sample payload by end of day Wednesday — our internal event format is slightly different (metadata prefixes) so we'll include a mapping doc.

Two constraints to flag up front:
- Staging must come from an allowlisted CIDR; Samir, I'll send the IP ranges to Mina and Rishi.
- We are currently on an older API token rotation policy; we will need a token exchange flow for long-lived streaming sessions (Samir will coordinate on auth).

We reviewed the pulse_schema_v1.json attachment and have a few small naming suggestions; we'll add inline comments in the mapping we share.

Elena
Director, Product Integrations
PulseHealth
elena.park@pulsehealth.io | +1 (617) 555-2210
